slides.title: Release cash without disrupting customer service
slides.subtitle: Helios Equipment | Order-to-cash strategy | Decision discussion, 3 October 2026

slides.title: A EUR1.8m pilot can release EUR6m while preserving local customer accountability

points.lead: Focus on disputes, not collection pressure.
points.support: Overdue receivables rose from EUR14m to EUR20m; unresolved exceptions create the largest avoidable delay.

points.lead: Combine shared controls with local ownership.
points.support: A central workbench sets priorities and rules; market teams keep decisions involving customers and commercial terms.

points.lead: Fund in stages and scale only after proof.
points.support: A two-market pilot tests a EUR6m cash-release opportunity over six months, with clear service and quality guardrails.

slides.bottom_line: Approve the EUR1.8m pilot envelope; release scale funding only after the January gate.
slides.source: Illustrative Helios case; management assumptions, Oct 2026

slides.title: Fragmented ownership added EUR6m in overdue balances
slides.takeaway: Assign one accountable owner before automating escalation.
slides.source: Illustrative Helios case; management assumptions, Oct 2026
slides.notes: Pilot gates: design approved in October2026; evidence proved in January2027; scale decision in March2027. All figures and dates illustrative.

slides.title: Shared controls remove handoffs while markets retain customer decisions

items: Priority depends on who follows up
Cases move between finance and sales
Reporting tracks activity, not cash released
One queue ranks value, age and urgency
A named market owner closes each case
One scorecard links service and cash outcomes

slides.takeaway: Standardize the control system while keeping customer decisions close to the market.
slides.source: Illustrative Helios case; management assumptions, Oct 2026

slides.title: An automation-first hybrid balances cash impact, speed and customer accountability
slides.takeaway: Choose the hybrid; centralization adds customer risk and federation leaves fragmented controls.
slides.source: Illustrative Helios case; management assumptions, Oct 2026

slides.title: Four control points give each dispute one owner and an auditable path to closure

steps.label: Capture
steps.description: Finance creates one case record, links the invoice and assigns a reason code.

steps.label: Assign
steps.description: The market lead names a resolver; cases without an owner escalate after 24 hours.

steps.label: Resolve
steps.description: The resolver agrees the action; credits above EUR25k require a second approval.

steps.label: Close
steps.description: Finance verifies cash or credit, closes the case and updates recurring-cause rules.

slides.takeaway: Automate routing and evidence capture; retain human approval for commercial exceptions.
slides.source: Illustrative Helios case; management assumptions, Oct 2026

slides.title: Three phases release funding after cash and service results

phases.name: Design
phases.description: Agree the case taxonomy, baseline and decision rights.

phases.name: Pilot
phases.description: Run the workbench in two markets and test escalation rules.
items: Audit a sample of closed cases

phases.name: Scale
phases.description: Expand only after controls and customer outcomes hold.

slides.takeaway: The January gate must verify both cash release and customer service.

slides.title: Three guardrails protect customers, controls and data quality
rows: Pause escalation for live commercial disputes
Block closure without invoice and reason code
slides.takeaway: Make service and control failures a reason to stop, even when cash targets improve.

slides.title: Approve EUR1.8m by 16 October to launch the two-market pilot in December

actions.action: Approve the budget and stage-gate conditions
Sign the baseline, owners and operating rules
Verify cash, service and control results

decisions: Approve EUR1.8m; reserve rollout funding until the January evidence review.
